definition: Voice portals are the voice equivalent of web portals, giving access to information through spoken commands and voice responses.
details: Ideally a voice portal could be an access point for any type of information, services, or transactions found on the Internet. Common uses include movie time listings and stock trading. In telecommunications circles, voice portals may be referred to as interactive voice response (IVR) systems, but this term also includes DTMF services. With the emergence of conversational assistants such as Apple's Siri, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Microsoft Cortana, and Samsung's Bixby, Voice Portals can now be accessed through mobile devices and Far Field voice smart speakers such as the Amazon Echo and Google Home.

explainer.lead: A voice portal is a spoken-command access point to information and services, the voice equivalent of a web portal. It matters because it delivers content and transactions over the phone without a screen.

tiers.eli5: It's like a website you talk to instead of looking at.
tiers.practitioner: Developers build them on speech recognition plus text-to-speech, routing spoken requests to back-end information or transaction services; a pitfall is that users cannot scan options visually, so prompt design must anticipate what people will say.
tiers.paperLevel: A voice portal provides access to information, services, or transactions through spoken commands and voice responses; in telecom it overlaps with interactive voice response, which also includes DTMF services. Its practical limits are those of the recogniser and the menu or dialogue design.

explainer.example: A caller asks a voice portal for movie showtimes and hears the listing read back.
